transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, on Corova Coleman, three media organizations say some
of their staffers were denied entry to the White House this morning.
That's even though a federal judge ruled overnight, the White House must restore access to CNN,
MS Now, and Politico.
The group sued after President Trump banned them because they "purposely write negative
news."
Here's NPR's David Fulkenflick.
NPR's David Fulkenflick reporting.
All this is unfolding as President Trump is preparing to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping
on a state visit.
Trump will host a state dinner for Xi tonight at the White House.
Trump and Xi are expected to discuss the tense trade relationship between their countries.
Since May, the Food and Drug Administration has been without a confirmed commissioner.
That could soon change.
Today, the president's nominee to fill the position will be on Capitol Hill for her confirmation
hearing.
NPR's Sydney Lupkin reports.
Dr. Heidi Overton will be in the hot seat as senators from the Committee on Health,
Education, Labor and Pensions question her qualifications to be the next commissioner
of the FDA.
Dr. Marty McCarry resigned back in May.
Overton currently works in the White House.
Before that, she worked at the conservative America First Policy Institute.
She was in the Oval Office when President Trump issued a controversial executive order
pushing to change the childhood vaccine schedule and dredging up debunked theories linking
vaccines to autism.
Speaking at the press conference, Overton called Trump's order a historic action.
At least one prominent Democrat, Senator Patty Murray of Washington, has already said she
will vote no.
Sydney Lupkin, NPR News.
Stocks open lower this morning as bond yields jump and PR Scott Horsley reports the Dow
was dropped 140 points.
Investors are demanding higher returns on long-term government debt amid stubborn inflation.
The yield on 30-year treasuries reached a 22-year high, while the yield on 10-year treasuries
is hovering above 5 percent.
The 10-year treasury is closely tied to commercial loan products like mortgages, and suggests
the interest rate on home loans could soon top 7 percent.
The president of the Cleveland Federal Reserve Bank warns the longer inflation remains elevated,
the more costly it may be to bring prices under control.
The central bank raised its benchmark interest rate last week, and investors expect at least
one additional rate hike this year.
And Starbucks says it's closing 250 underperforming stores in North America this week.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
This is NPR.
A hurricane watch is up for the big island of Hawaii as Tropical Storm Nolo gets closer.
Forecasters don't think it will make landfall, but they're expecting parts of Hawaii will
get more than two feet of rain.
This comes as Hawaii government leaders say they need more than $1 billion to recover
from an earthquake and devastating storms earlier this year.
Former tech executive Elizabeth Holmes is set to be released early from federal prison.
As NPR's Bobby Allen reports, Holmes was given an 11-year sentence in 2022 after a jury convicted
her of fraud.
Holmes ran the blood-testing startup Theranos that was once the darling of Silicon Valley.
But a jury found she defrauded investors out of hundreds of millions of dollars by deceiving
them that Theranos could revolutionize health care with just a pinprick of blood.
Her prison sentence had been reduced several times.
She was scheduled to be released in 2030.
A new notice sent to Holmes, investor victims from the Bureau of Prisons, shows she is set
to be moved to a halfway house next year.
It's unclear what led to her partial freedom.
Holmes has been trending online since comedian Nathan Fielder premiered a documentary called
You Can See Everything, in which Holmes and her family let Fielder live with them in the
weeks before she turned herself in.
Bobby Allen, NPR News.
Just in, lawyers for the three media outlets that had their White House press passes revoked,
CNN, MS Now and Politico, have now asked a federal court for an immediate hearing.
They say that the White House has turned away journalists for the three outlets this morning.
You're listening to NPR.
Want to hear this podcast without sponsor breaks?
Amazon Prime members can listen to NPR News Now, sponsor free through Amazon Music.
Or you can also support NPR's vital journalism and get NPR+ at plus.npr.org.
That's plus.npr.org.
